data.title: Pentavalent antimonials (sodium stibogluconate, meglumine antimoniate)
data.summary: Other antiparasitics · Pentavalent antimony (SbV) compounds; antileishmanial
data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Other antiparasitics_

**Class:** Pentavalent antimony (SbV) compounds; antileishmanial

## Mechanism of action
- Prodrug: SbV reduced to trivalent SbIII inside macrophages and amastigotes
- Inhibits trypanothione reductase and parasite glycolysis/fatty acid oxidation → amastigote death; also enhances macrophage killing

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Cutaneous leishmaniasis: intralesional for small, few lesions (Old World — L. tropica, L. major); systemic for multiple, large, facial/joint lesions, lymphatic spread, mucosal or New World species
- Mucocutaneous and visceral leishmaniasis (visceral: largely replaced in India by liposomal amphotericin B/miltefosine because of resistance in Bihar)
- Post-kala-azar dermal leishmaniasis (older regimens; miltefosine now preferred)

## Dose & formulations
- Systemic: 20 mg SbV/kg/day IV or IM for 20 days (cutaneous) or 28 days (mucosal/visceral)
- Intralesional: 0.2–1 mL (100 mg SbV/mL) infiltrated until the lesion blanches, weekly or every 2 weeks for 3–8 sessions (often combined with cryotherapy)
- Sodium stibogluconate 100 mg SbV/mL; meglumine antimoniate 85 mg SbV/mL

## Adverse effects
- Cardiotoxicity: QT prolongation, T-wave changes, arrhythmia — dose and duration related
- Pancreatitis (raised amylase/lipase), hepatitis, nephrotoxicity
- Myalgia, arthralgia, fatigue, headache; cytopenias
- IL: pain, swelling, local reactions

## Contraindications
- Heart disease (prolonged QT), significant renal/hepatic disease, pregnancy

## Drug interactions
- Other QT-prolonging drugs (amiodarone, macrolides, fluoroquinolones, antipsychotics)

## Monitoring
- ECG twice weekly (stop if QTc >500 ms), amylase/lipase, LFT, renal function, CBC weekly

## Pregnancy & lactation
Avoid (systemic); prefer local measures or liposomal amphotericin B.

## Viva points
- SbV prodrug → SbIII
- 20 mg SbV/kg/day × 20 days (cutaneous)
- ECG monitoring — QT prolongation
- Resistance in Bihar → replaced for kala-azar

_Sources: Khopkar ch.5 (Antileishmanial agents — sodium stibogluconate); Wolverton 4e ch.12. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
